content:
Apple yesterday released iOS 27 beta 5, with changes including new app icons and minor Spotlight design tweaks. As it turns out, the update also contains code for all the new iPhone models expected to launch in the next six to eight months.

Unreleased iPhone codenames

As first discovered by Macworld, iOS 27 beta 5 references six unreleased iPhones, covering the entire iPhone 18 lineup, the iPhone Air 2, and the upcoming foldable iPhone Ultra. These codenames were found within "system files related to iPhone battery drivers and Battery Intelligence features."

The code only references Apple's internal identifiers (such as V62, V63, etc.), and does not contain marketing names. However, based on other leaks, these model identifiers can be matched to their expected market names as follows:

  • V62: iPhone Air 2
  • V63: iPhone 18 Pro
  • V64: iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • V67: iPhone 18
  • V68: iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Fold)
  • V69: iPhone 18e

This update does not contain further information about these devices. Apple is expected to kick off the iPhone 18 cycle next month with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The iPhone Ultra is also expected to be announced next month.

The iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 are reportedly slated to launch sometime in early 2027. This marks the first year of Apple's reorganized iPhone release schedule, splitting launches throughout the year into two windows.

Which upcoming iPhone model are you most looking forward to from Apple? Are you interested in the iPhone Ultra? Let us know in the comments.
